text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated error rate and CPU pressure on inference-serving (toolcall + structured-output routes). Multiple tenants seeing 5xxs and timeouts. Pager triggered for SRE team.
lee: seeing 50% spike in worker latencies, GPU utilization at 95% on cluster-east-2. Tool invocation queue building.
maya: confirmed — toolcall worker pool hosts 12/16 overloaded, KV cache thrash. Affected endpoints: /v1/invoke/tool, /v1/chat/structured (stream).
sam: paging runbook step 1: scope and isolate noisy tenants. Any obvious noisy tenant ids?
lee: top offenders: tenant-42, tenant-ml-demo, tenant-free-tier-7. They account for ~68% of toolcall QPS.
ops: I'm going to apply a soft tenant-level throttle on free-tier first. Will also push a temporary route rule to favour text-only fallback for non-critical callers.
maya: propose immediate mitigation: 1) set global toolcall concurrency cap to 8 per host 2) downgrade structured-output feature flag to text-only for public tier 3) add 10s per-tenant cooldown for repeated tool calls.
lee: +1. Also suggest enabling short-circuit KV-prefix caching for chat sessions to reduce repeated prefixes.
ops: doing step 1 now — running control plane API: 
```
curl -X POST "https://controlplane.internal.redwood/v1/mitigations/apply" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{"action":"set_route_limit","route":"/v1/invoke/tool","limit":8}'
```
deploy-bot: deploy started for mitigation policy 2026-03-17T22:05Z (policy-id: mig-176660).
karen-cs: heads up — customer impact: two enterprise customers reported degraded completions, CS is drafting a notification. We should avoid blanket disable for paid tiers.
lee: confirmed — plan: target free and demo tiers first. Paid/dedicated should keep toolcall but with reduced concurrency and queue priorities.
maya: implementing structured-output feature-flag flip for public plane: setting structured_output=off for plan=free, demo. Command: 
```
PATCH /internal/featureflags/structured_output
Body: {"targets":[{"plan":"free","value":false},{"plan":"demo","value":false}],"reason":"emergency-load-mitigation"}
```
sam: applied per-tenant cooldown for tenant-free-tier-7 and tenant-ml-demo. Their QPS dropped ~80% after 2m.
lee: GPU pressure dropping to 80% now, latencies improving. Still seeing intermittent 502s on toolhost-7.
ops: adding route-level rate limit for streaming structured responses to 5 RPS per IP (edge). Edge rule applied.
leo: added a temporary throttling policy for the /v1/chat/structured stream: max_tokens_per_minute=2000 for free/demo.
karen-cs: draft customer message for affected demos done. pinged legal for wording on paid customers.
maya: starting canary rollback plan: if cluster metrics stable for 10m, gradually re-enable structured output for demo then free.
lee: monitoring: 10m window observational metrics look good — error rate down from 6.8% -> 1.2%, mean p95 latency down 40%.
sam: filing follow-up postmortem ticket: PM-4938, marking mitigation steps and tenant actions.
ops: leaving retention rules in place for 30m, then we'll reassess. I'll hand off to night oncall in 45m.
lee: if anything spikes, escalate to infra and open an incident bridge. For now marking this as "active mitigation".
maya: note — we intentionally did not disable toolcall for paid dedicated clusters; internal telemetry shows no customer SLA breaches there.
leo: added short snippet to runbook for future: prefer feature-flag flip for structured output over full disable. Saves latency and UX.
karen-cs: will update affected customers in #customer-notify and send targeted emails.
deploy-bot: mitigation policy mig-176660 applied successfully across 6/6 regions.
ops: handing off to night oncall @lee_night — summary posted in ops-runbook channel. Leaving health check alert at 10m cadence.
lee: thanks team. :thumbsup: I'll follow up with a consolidated incident note later and start the timeline draft.
incident-bot: Incident flagged: SVC-2026-1342 (toolcall overload) — assigned to lee, maya. Severity: Sev3 (service degradation).
lee: handoff complete, closing thread for active ops work. If anything new pops up, reopen or @channel.
